# Complete PCB Design Workflow with EasyEDA

## Your Primary Tool: EasyEDA ✅
Since you've already selected EasyEDA as your PCB design platform, let's build a complete workflow around it with the right complementary tools.

---

## What EasyEDA Already Covers

Before identifying gaps, here's what EasyEDA handles natively:

| Capability | Coverage |
|---|---|
| Schematic Capture | ✅ Built-in |
| PCB Layout | ✅ Built-in |
| SPICE Simulation | ✅ Built-in |
| Design Rule Check (DRC) | ✅ Built-in |
| Electrical Rule Check (ERC) | ✅ Built-in |
| 3D View | ✅ Built-in |
| Gerber Export | ✅ Built-in |
| BOM Export | ✅ Built-in |
| Auto-Routing | ✅ Built-in |
| Cloud Integration | ✅ Built-in |
| Up to 16 layers | ✅ Built-in |
| Library (up to 1M footprints) | ✅ Built-in |

> **Key insight:** EasyEDA is quite self-contained, but gaps remain in **signal integrity validation**, **trace width/impedance calculations**, and **component parametric calculations** — all critical for a professional workflow.

---

## Identified Workflow Gaps & Recommended Complementary Tools

### 🔧 Gap 1: Trace Width & Current Capacity Validation

EasyEDA does not calculate trace widths for current handling. You need external calculators:

#### **Option A — Omni Calculator PCB Trace Width Calculator**
- Uses **IPC-2141A standards**
- Calculates: trace width, resistance, voltage drop, power loss, temperature rise
- Covers both **internal and external PCB layers**
- Best for: general-purpose trace sizing

#### **Option B — Circuit Digest PCB Trace Width Calculator**
- Uses **IPC-2221 standards** (slightly older but widely accepted)
- Calculates: copper area, cross-sectional area, voltage drop
- Best for: manufacturing-focused designs

> 💡 **Tip:** Use **Omni Calculator** for day-to-day work and **Circuit Digest** as a cross-check, since they use different IPC standards.

---

### 🔧 Gap 2: Impedance Control for High-Speed Signals

If your design includes USB, HDMI, RF, or any differential pairs, controlled impedance is mandatory.

#### **Option A — Technick PCB Impedance Calculator** *(Top Recommendation)*
- Supports: Microstrip, Embedded Microstrip, Stripline, Dual Stripline, Asymmetric Stripline
- Covers **differential impedance** for both Microstrip and Stripline
- Best for: USB, Ethernet, high-speed digital signals

#### **Option B — Skottans Elektronik Impedance Calculator**
- Calculates: Z₀, C₀ (capacitance), and **signal propagation delay (t_pd)**
- Unique advantage: propagation delay calculation aids timing analysis
- Best for: timing-sensitive designs

#### **Option C — Saturn PCB Design Toolkit** *(Most Comprehensive)*
- **Downloadable tool** with the broadest feature set:
  - Microstrip/Stripline impedance
  - Via current capacity and impedance
  - Crosstalk analysis
  - Planar inductor calculations
  - Thermal resistance estimation
  - BGA land calculations
  - Skin depth and signal bandwidth
- Best for: advanced or professional designs requiring all-in-one analysis

> 💡 **Recommendation:** Download **Saturn PCB Design Toolkit** as your primary engineering calculator — it replaces multiple standalone calculators.

---

### 🔧 Gap 3: Passive Component Calculations

Before placing components in EasyEDA, verify their values analytically:

#### **For Capacitors:**
- **Apexwaves** — Capacitance calculation and parameter verification

#### **For Inductors:**
- **coil32** — Inductance and coil dimensioning
- **Eeweb** — Quick inductance calculations
- **Saturn PCB Toolkit** — Also covers planar inductors on PCB

> 💡 **Tip:** Always verify inductor values before routing — coil geometry directly affects your PCB footprint dimensions.

---

### 🔧 Gap 4: LED Circuit Design

If your design includes LED arrays or indicator LEDs:

| Tool | Best Use Case |
|---|---|
| **DIGIKEY LED Calculator** | Professional-grade, links to component sourcing |
| **LEDCALCULATOR.NET** | Series/parallel LED configuration planning |
| **LEDMATRIX-EDITOR** | Visual LED matrix design + Arduino pattern generation |
| **ALLABOUTCIRCUITS** | Quick LED resistor calculations |

---

### 🔧 Gap 5: Power Supply Design

If your PCB includes switching regulators or converters:

- **ON Semiconductor Design Tools** — Simulation, topology selection, component selection, thermal analysis
- Best for: SMPS, buck/boost converters, regulators
- Complements EasyEDA's SPICE simulation for power stage verification

---

```
PHASE 1: PRE-DESIGN ENGINEERING
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ├── Calculate trace widths → Omni Calculator / Circuit Digest
  ├── Calculate impedance targets → Technick or Skottans
  ├── Verify passive values → Apexwaves (caps), coil32 (inductors)
  ├── Design LED circuits → DigiKey / LEDCALCULATOR.NET
  └── Power supply topology → ON Semiconductor Design Tools

PHASE 2: SCHEMATIC DESIGN (EasyEDA)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ├── Create schematic using EasyEDA's schematic editor
  ├── Use EasyEDA's library (up to 1M footprints)
  ├── Run ERC (Electrical Rule Check)

PHASE 3: PCB LAYOUT (EasyEDA)

  ├── Import netlist from schematic
  ├── Apply pre-calculated trace widths from Phase 1
  ├── Apply impedance-controlled routing for high-speed signals

  └── Review 3D View for physical clearance

PHASE 4: VERIFICATION & VALIDATION
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ├── Cross-check impedance → Saturn PCB Toolkit
  ├── Verify crosstalk margins → Saturn PCB Toolkit
  ├── Confirm thermal estimates → Saturn PCB Toolkit
  └── Final DRC pass in EasyEDA

PHASE 5: OUTPUT & MANUFACTURING
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  ├── Export Gerber files (EasyEDA)

## Identified Gaps & Recommended Complementary Tools

### 🔧 Gap 1: PCB Trace Width & Current Capacity Calculations

EasyEDA does not include built-in trace width calculators based on IPC standards. Before routing, you need to validate trace dimensions for your current requirements.

#### **Recommended: Omni Calculator PCB Trace Width Calculator**
- **Type:** Online platform (free)
- **Why:** Implements IPC-2141A standards, calculates trace width for specified current, and provides resistance, voltage drop, power loss, and temperature rise for both internal and external layers
- **When to use:** During pre-routing planning phase

#### **Alternative: Circuit Digest PCB Trace Width Calculator**
- **Why:** Uses IPC-2221 standards — provides copper area and cross-sectional area data in addition to standard parameters
- **Best for:** High-current power traces where detailed copper geometry matters

---

### 🔧 Gap 2: Impedance Control for High-Speed/RF Traces

EasyEDA has no native impedance calculator for controlled-impedance traces (e.g., USB, SPI, RF transmission lines).

#### **Recommended: Saturn PCB Design Toolkit**
- **Type:** Free download
- **Why:** The most comprehensive calculator in the ecosystem — covers microstrip, stripline, differential pair impedance, via current capacity, crosstalk analysis, thermal resistance, skin depth, and more — all in one tool
- **Strengths:**
  - Covers virtually every PCB parameter calculation needed
  - Differential pair support (critical for USB, HDMI, Ethernet)
  - Via impedance and current capacity
  - Planar inductor calculations
  - Unit conversion utilities
- **Limitation:** Windows desktop application only
- **When to use:** During stack-up planning and high-speed trace routing

#### **Alternative: Technick PCB Impedance Calculator or Skottans Elektronik**
- **Why:** Web-based, instantly accessible, covers microstrip/stripline/differential configurations
- **Best for:** Quick impedance checks without installing software

---

### 🔧 Gap 3: Passive Component Value Verification

For designs involving inductors or capacitors with specific value requirements, EasyEDA doesn't provide component-level design calculators.

#### **For Inductors — Recommended: coil32**
- **Type:** Free online calculator
- **Why:** Provides inductance calculation and coil dimensioning — essential when designing custom inductors or validating datasheet values

#### **Alternatives for Inductors:**
| Tool | Best For |
|---|---|
| **Eeweb** | Quick online inductance checks |
| **All About Circuits** | Educational context + calculation |
| **66pacific** | RF coil design |
| **steam-engine** | Stepper motor / coil applications |

#### **For Capacitors — Recommended: Apexwaves**
- **Type:** Free online calculator
- **Why:** Capacitance calculation and related parameters — useful for bypass/decoupling capacitor validation

---

### 🔧 Gap 4: LED Circuit Design

If your PCB includes LED arrays or indicator LEDs, dedicated calculators simplify resistor sizing.

#### **Recommended: DIGIKEY LED Calculator**
- **Why:** From a trusted component supplier — directly links calculation results to purchasable components
- **Covers:** LED resistor calculation for series/parallel configurations

#### **For LED Matrix Designs:**
| Tool | Function |
|---|---|
| **LEDMATRIX-EDITOR** | Visual matrix pattern design, Arduino integration |
| **LEDCALCULATOR.NET** | Series/parallel LED configuration |
| **HEBEILTD** | Multi-LED string calculations |

---

### 🔧 Gap 5: Power Supply & SMPS Design

If your board includes switching power supplies or regulators, EasyEDA's SPICE simulation is helpful but not sufficient for topology selection and thermal analysis.

#### **Recommended: ON Semiconductor Design Tools**
- **Type:** Online platform
- **Why:** Covers simulation, topology selection, component selection, and thermal analysis for SMPS designs — fills a significant gap for power electronics boards
- **When to use:** During power stage design before bringing the schematic into EasyEDA

---

### 🔧 Gap 6: Design Portability / Backup Tool

EasyEDA is cloud-dependent. Having a compatible offline tool provides resilience and design portability.

#### **Recommended: KiCad** *(I/O Compatible with EasyEDA)*
- **Type:** Free download
- **Why:** EasyEDA can export to KiCad-compatible formats; KiCad offers offline capability, strong community support, and is I/O compatible
- **Key Features:** DRC, ERC, SPICE simulation, Gerber export, 3D view, cross-platform (Windows/Mac/Linux), up to 32 layers
- **Limitation:** Steeper learning curve than EasyEDA
- **When to use:** For complex designs, offline work, or when more advanced routing features are needed

#### **Alternative: EAGLE** *(I/O Compatible with EasyEDA)*
- **Why:** EasyEDA can import Eagle designs; useful for teams already in the Autodesk ecosystem
- **Note:** Paid subscription for most professional features

│   ├── Calculate impedance targets for high-speed nets

├── Draw schematic using EasyEDA editor
├── Run ERC (Electrical Rule Check)
├── Run SPICE simulation to verify circuit behavior
└── Generate netlist

├── Apply impedance-controlled routing parameters

## 💡 Practical Tips for Success

### Phase 1–2: Schematic & Simulation
> 💡 Always simulate **before** layout. Catching a wrong capacitor value in simulation is free; catching it after fabrication costs time and money.

- Start with a **hierarchical schematic** for complex designs to keep things organized
- Use **net labels** liberally — they reduce clutter and make the schematic easier to read
- Run **CircuitMaker's Monte Carlo analysis** for tolerance-sensitive analog designs

### Phase 3: ERC
> 💡 Never skip ERC — even experienced designers find it catches overlooked unconnected pins.

- Resolve **every warning**, not just errors — warnings often indicate real design issues
- Verify **power pin directions** match your component symbols

### Phase 4: Calculators
> 💡 Use **Saturn PCB Design Toolkit** as your go-to — it covers the most calculations in one interface, downloadable and offline capable.

- For **power traces**: assume at least **2× the calculated minimum** width for thermal margin
- For **high-speed signals**: calculate impedance with your **specific PCB stackup** — manufacturer stackup datasheets are essential inputs

### Phase 5: Layout
> 💡 The golden rule: **placement determines 80% of your routing quality.** Spend extra time here.

- Route **power and ground planes first**, then critical high-speed signals, then everything else
- Keep **decoupling capacitors** as close as physically possible to IC power pins
- **Avoid right-angle traces** for high-frequency signals — use 45° bends
- Import manufacturer **design rule files** if available to pre-set DRC constraints
- Use **copper pours** for ground planes to minimize impedance and EMI

### Phase 6: 3D Verification
> 💡 Import a 3D model of your enclosure in STEP format to check for real-world fit before fabricating.

- Validate **connector clearances** — mechanical conflicts with enclosures are a common, costly mistake
- Check **component height** against your stackup height

### Phase 7: DRC
> 💡 Run DRC with your **manufacturer's design rules loaded** — generic defaults often allow dimensions that your fab house can't produce reliably.

- Pay close attention to **minimum annular ring** and **drill-to-copper** clearance
- Check **silkscreen-to-pad** clearances to avoid unreadable legends

### Phase 8: Manufacturing Files
> 💡 Always submit Gerbers to a **free online Gerber viewer** (e.g., GerbLook or PCBShopper) before uploading to your fab house to catch export errors.

**Gerber Layer Checklist:**
```
✔ F.Cu      — Front copper layer
✔ B.Cu      — Back copper layer
✔ In*.Cu    — Internal copper layers (if multilayer)
✔ F.Mask    — Front solder mask
✔ B.Mask    — Back solder mask
✔ F.Silkscreen — Front silkscreen
✔ B.Silkscreen — Back silkscreen (optional)
✔ Edge.Cuts — Board outline
✔ *.drl     — Excellon drill file
✔ BOM       — Bill of Materials
✔ PnP       — Pick and Place (for SMT assembly)
```
